items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Now when you say that, Mitty, what would the band have to have for you to consider it a real old time band?

ctx.x: Let's see. Let's see. Let's see. Let's see. Break right into the blues. Yeah. Break into the blues and that way. But really now, how the band plays, well it's really funny to me. Sometimes I sit down and look and think how much the band has changed now. And really I would like to see a real old time band.
Now when you say that, Mitty, what would the band have to have for you to consider it a real old time band? Would you explain how it would sound?

Well I think it sounds good. Let's include violin leading. You see, you wouldn't have to have the piano, with the old time orchestra, which they called would be piano. But in the meantime you wouldn't have to have piano for an old time band. Because just to see if they could, how would it sound different between now and then? Now and then. Man, that sounds funny.
